solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lost to antiquity, like husband's boring hat

indicators.note: the like-and-husband pair drills its way into the middle of the archaic word

parts.note: lorn is an archaic word for lost or forsaken, hence 'to antiquity'
EG, short for 'for example', stands in for 'like'
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A hat, like the one a husband wears, has disappeared into the distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: A leghorn is a hat of fine plaited straw, named after the Italian port. It also sets the theme: Foghorn Leghorn is the cartoon rooster.
explanation.definitionFit: A leghorn is a broad-brimmed straw hat made from Italian wheat straw.

clue.text: Caps taken off for it, dropped lawsuit

parts.note: to lower is to drop, and lower can be read as a past state
a case is a legal action in court

explanation.surface: Someone takes their cap off on hearing that a legal action has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Caps here means capital letters; removing them gives small letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowercase letters are the small ones used when capital letters are removed from text.

clue.text: Giant split within set

indicators.note: the word for split goes inside the word for set

parts.note: jelly that has set has gelled
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: A huge creature splits inside a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Grendel is the monstrous giant killed by the hero in the Old English poem Beowulf.

clue.text: See 13
Votes against heir moving up

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a son is the traditional heir

explanation.surface: Ballots are cast against an heir's promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Noes are negative votes in a ballot or division, counted against a motion.

clue.text: Drink hot date introduced to idiot twins (who shall be nameless)

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: the two letters are brought in ahead of each copy of the trimmed word
nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name, so each copy loses that letter
twins means the word for idiot appears twice

parts.note: numpty is Scottish slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A romantic evening ends in drinks with a pair of foolish siblings whose names are kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who shall be nameless' looks like coy discretion but means drop the letter for name. Numpty is Scottish slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old drink of ale boiled with brandy, besides being the egg of the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Head-turning splendour of Hollywood topcoat

indicators.note: the two letters at the head of the word swap round

parts.note: luster is the American spelling of lustre, meaning splendour

explanation.surface: A striking coat with all the glamour of Tinseltown.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose overcoat, often with a cape, originally made in Ireland.

clue.text: Initially holding post in retirement, Kamala is irritable

indicators.note: post means after, putting that letter at the end
retiring is withdrawing, so the title goes backwards

parts.note: Kamala Harris was US vice-president, colloquially the veep
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of holding is all that is used

parts.note: only its opening letter is wanted here

explanation.surface: A former vice-president, now retired, is cranky about holding a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job, but it is the Latin for after.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish means easily annoyed and petulant.

clue.text: It's very alarming indeed about Mika's gut

indicators.note: the word for indeed goes round the extracted letters

parts.note: yes as an emphatic agreement

indicators.note: to gut is to take out the insides, so only the middle of the name is used

parts.note: the possessive points to the name Mika itself

explanation.surface: A frightened cry about the state of a person named Mika's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Yikes is an exclamation of alarm or shock.

clue.text: Smart-arse gets this wrong, missing his stellar shift

indicators.note: the remaining letters are put in a wrong, jumbled order
the three letters of his are dropped from the combined fodder

parts.note: the know-all's label supplies its letters as written
taken as written and added to the know-all
taken as written, the letters to drop

explanation.surface: A know-all makes a mistake, missing a star's movement in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A star stream is a group of stars moving together through the galaxy, a stellar drift.

clue.text: Twist away with ease

parts.note: rest and ease both mean relaxation

explanation.surface: A tip for turning something off easily.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to pull or wrench something from someone with a twisting force.

clue.text: Sort of lush, very large, mountain

parts.note: a lush is a drunkard, as is a sot
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a peak is a mountain or its summit

explanation.surface: A rough description of a drunk, a hulking great mountain of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are verbal hedges, signalling that a word is used loosely or approximately.

clue.text: Hound my counterpart in Pravda?

definitions.meaning: a breed of gundog, the Irish breed with a chestnut coat
the setter speaking: a crossword compiler at the Soviet Communist newspaper would be a Red one

explanation.surface: A setter asks whether to pursue the opposite number who compiles puzzles for the Soviet paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Pravda was the Communist Party newspaper of the USSR, and Red is shorthand for a communist; setter is what crossword compilers are called.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish red setter is a well-known gundog breed, and the phrase also reads as a communist compiler.

clue.text: 24a 25. A question of order some other Across answers fail to resolve

definitions.meaning: the two Across answers form the opening of a famous question about which of two things preceded the other

definitions.text: some other Across answers fail to resolve
definitions.meaning: the grid offers a hen-related hat and cartoon rooster plus a nursery-rhyme egg, without settling the priority

explanation.walkthrough: The full phrase is 'Which came first, the chicken or the egg?' In the grid, LEGHORN and FOGHORN (Foghorn Leghorn) give the chicken and HUMPTY DUMPTY the egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial causality dilemma asks whether the bird or its egg existed earlier.

clue.text: Chap heading west almost left port

indicators.note: in an across clue, westward is right to left, so the letters run backwards
the past tense stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a ship that left port sailed

explanation.surface: A man travelling west has very nearly put out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is a man's name, the Greek form of Elijah, so it is one particular male person.

clue.text: A line on river-dweller withdrawing rather briskly

parts.note: taken as written
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the animal backs away, so its letters run in reverse

parts.note: the otter lives along rivers

explanation.surface: A fishing line is cast at an otter, which hurries away rather quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field, so on gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is the musical tempo marking meaning fairly brisk, slightly slower than allegro.

clue.text: Weapon curiously vanished, as has Dean

indicators.note: Dean has vanished from the mix too, so his letters are removed

parts.note: curiously signals an odd rearrangement of the letters of vanished, putting the four letters of the name at the end
the name taken as written, the letters that vanish

explanation.surface: A knife has mysteriously gone missing, and so has a man named Dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vanished' looks like the verb of the story but it is the letters to mix; Dean is the one who disappears from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiv is slang for a knife, especially an improvised blade made in prison.

clue.text: Tiddly dipping into wine cask, get cards

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits inside the wine and the cask

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a tun is a large barrel

indicators.note: tiddly means tipsy, so the letters of get stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the word to scramble

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker raids the wine barrel and then fetches a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Vingt-et-un is the card game also known as pontoon or blackjack.

clue.text: Safeguard when posting second win

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, a second
to bag something is to win or secure it

explanation.surface: A careful sender protects a parcel, scoring a quick victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jiffy bag is a padded envelope that protects items sent through the post.

clue.text: Paradise Regained and Endymion at their unified core

indicators.note: run the two titles together as one word and take the letters at the centre, either side of the join

parts.note: its closing pair of letters sits at the join when the two titles are run together
its opening pair of letters sits at the join with the other title

explanation.surface: A literary remark about Milton's Paradise Regained and Keats's Endymion sharing a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Run the two titles together and the four letters at the middle straddle the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the garden of Genesis, the biblical original of paradise on earth.

clue.text: Pointed remark investigator found cutting spread to the north

indicators.note: the detective cuts into the reversed spread
in a down clue, heading north means reading upward

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A sharp comment from a detective who found a spread being cut up north.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying with a sharp, pithy point.

clue.text: I'm loving this sweet German wine: we sent empties here?

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight, as if saying I'm loving this
lieb is German for dear or sweet, the German context carrying over

indicators.note: sent says the letters of we are sent away from the wine word

parts.note: Wein is the German word for wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone delighted with sweet German wine sends off the empty bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: WEIN with WE sent away leaves IN; LIEB is German for dear or sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelie bin is a large wheeled rubbish container, where empty bottles end up.

clue.text: Variety of flour tortilla (a lot full to bursting from it!), but folding over

definitions.text: Variety of flour tortilla (a lot full to bursting from it!), but folding over

indicators.note: the word but folds itself around the remaining letters

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: Variety of flour tortilla (a lot full to bursting from it
parts.note: jumble the letters of flour tortilla, then let the letters of 'a lot full to' burst out of them: only the three letters left over are used
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A burrito is a stuffed flour tortilla folded over, packed so full it bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of 'a lot full to' from 'flour tortilla' and only three letters remain. The whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of a flour tortilla folded around a filling.

clue.text: Alfred, Peter or Catherine perhaps eliminated danger

indicators.note: the for-example letters are taken out

parts.note: each of these monarchs is known as 'the Great'
eg, for example, is signalled by perhaps

explanation.surface: A list of historical monarchs who perhaps eliminated a menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of danger or a menacing possibility of harm.

clue.text: That woman, she's enchanting to the ear

indicators.note: heard rather than seen, the spell-caster's name matches the answer

parts.note: a witch is a woman who casts spells, an enchantress

explanation.surface: Someone points out a woman who sounds bewitching.
explanation.walkthrough: Many speakers say the two words identically; this is also the first word of the theme's question.
explanation.definitionFit: Which and that are interchangeable relative pronouns introducing a clause.

clue.text: A little money United accepted no longer on record

indicators.note: the married couple takes the small sum inside

parts.note: to wed is to unite in marriage
I as the Roman numeral one, standing for a
P for a penny, the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A small sum was taken by a club no longer in the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club, as in Manchester United, but it means married.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiped tape or record has been erased, so its data no longer exists.

clue.text: Were leading actors entertaining author Douglas?

indicators.note: the actors play host to the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a cast is the company of actors in a production
the setter, as author of the puzzle, refers to themself as me
the Douglas fir is a tall conifer

explanation.surface: A question whether the stars of the show were hosting a writer called Douglas.
explanation.definitionFit: To come first is to be in the lead, ahead of everyone else in a race or ranking.

clue.text: Keep on alone, always probing

indicators.note: the word for always pokes into the Latin phrase

parts.note: per se means by itself, alone
ever in the sense of for ever

explanation.surface: Advice to carry on by yourself, forever investigating.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist or continue despite difficulty.

clue.text: Is it Germany's football team being mischievous?

definitions.meaning: a football team has eleven players, and the German word for eleven is the answer
a puckish sprite of folklore is known for its playful tricks

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether the German national side are behaving like naughty sprites.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small mischievous folklore creature, and the same spelling is German for the number eleven.

clue.text: The nearly men left in the crummy bits

indicators.note: left is placed inside the rearranged letters
crummy means shoddy or broken up, so the word bits is reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, the word to scramble

explanation.surface: The also-rans were left among the worthless scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: The B-list is the second tier of celebrities, those who almost reached the top rank.

clue.text: See 5
Swine and deer, young Spooner gives warning

indicators.note: Rev Spooner was known for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a fawn is a young deer

explanation.surface: A pig and a young deer, and the Reverend Spooner raises an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap works by sound: the second word becomes 'horn', not a spelling of the letters exchanged. Foghorn Leghorn is the cartoon rooster of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A foghorn is a loud horn sounded to warn ships in fog.
